notes: Impossible sensor readings (like 255 °C from a dead probe) are now ignored instead of polluting peaks and the verdict.
patch_notes: LibreHardwareMonitor sometimes publishes a physically impossible value for a missing probe — 255 °C or -55 °C where no sensor exists, or a fan RPM in the hundreds of thousands — and HeatWatch used to take it at face value, so one dead probe could fake a 255 °C peak and push the repaste verdict to "repaste". Temperatures outside -40…130 °C and fan speeds outside 0…100,000 RPM are now dropped at the parse step in all three readers (web feed, WMI, nvidia-smi), so they read as "no reading" instead: a dropped value never becomes a peak, a warning, or a verdict input, and the fallback sources still get their chance to fill the gap. A stopped fan at 0 RPM is real and is kept. New test round 23 covers the dropped values, the bounds, and the fallback; all 23 rounds pass.
